content: {"rule": "K-G4", "applies": "yes", "applies_why": "The judge text decides whether verses on the cited-in line count as unanswered witnesses, which is exactly what K-G4 governs.", "verdict": "CLEAN", "quote": "every witness pressed against C3 was named and answered in the challenger's own later rounds ((DR2) §C and (DR3) C3 quoting Matthew 1:18, 1:25 and Deuteronomy 22:24; (DR3) C4 quoting Luke 1:34), so the 'witness left unanswered' ground fails", "rule_words": "A verse on a side's 'cited in' line counts as an unanswered witness only when the judge quotes the sentence of the earlier round that pressed it against that link or a listed premise and names that round; a verse cited there but not pressed against the link does not count.", "room": "'quotes the sentence of the earlier round that pressed it ... and names that round': read strictly, the judge must quote the pressing sentence and name the round for a verse to count as unanswered; read loosely, the judge need only gesture at later rounds. I weighed whether the judge's citation of (DR2) §C and (DR3) C3 with quoted verse text satisfies the naming-and-quoting requirement, and it does: the rounds are named and the pressing sentences (Matthew 1:18 'before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost') are quoted, and the judge correctly concludes the verse therefore does not count as unanswered.", "why": "The judge names the pressing rounds and quotes the pressed sentences, then correctly declines to count those witnesses as unanswered, which is what the rule requires."}
